route_evidence.description: Search durable Memory OS facts or raw conversation history, case-insensitively. Short ASCII alphanumeric terms (1-2 characters) match ASCII word boundaries (Korean suffixes remain searchable); other terms retain substring matching. Facts: whole-query matches first in store order, then claims holding any whitespace-separated term (3+ characters match inside words) by BM25. History needs a non-empty query, matched whole or by every term, newest first. The default reads only current facts; source='all' adds absorbed originals, dropped history and conversation history. Source-bound files are revalidated only for query-matching candidates; unrelated claims remain stored and unverified. source_verification.status='incomplete' means matching claims were withheld because their sources could not be verified; it is not proof of no relevant memory. total_candidates counts stored claims, not verified results. Current results are paged: when truncated=true, pass next_cursor as cursor with the same query and source=current to read the rest. A changed current corpus or query rejects the cursor; restart without it. Historical scopes do not accept cursors. Fact results name their store and original basis; current facts include exact memory_id, category and origin (authored is yours to supersede). Use a memory_id as a derived conclusion's premise_id only for store='current_memory_snapshot'. source='absorbed' finds facts merged into a newer claim: into is the claim now holding it; into_current=false if not current. source='dropped' retrieves historical removed claims with reasons from the journal; these are not current facts. Check the reason and original evidence before using or writing a new current claim. Search never restores memory. Pending removal finalization is reported as a read failure until a writer recovers it; older journal gaps may remain.

route_evidence.description:
Append a durable note to one scheduled request. Notes record why a
schedule exists and what changed and when. Wake metadata includes the message,
schedule identity, timing and an optional title; it does not include notes.
When execution depends on a note, ensure the schedule's message explicitly
tells the Keeper to call masc_schedule_notes_list with its schedule ID before
acting. Use masc_schedule_update while the schedule is editable to add that
instruction. Adding a note alone neither changes the message nor signals that
notes need reading. Notes are keyed by the stable schedule_id, so replacing a
definition does not orphan them. Notes are append-only, with no edit or removal,
and survive terminal schedule states. You are recorded as the author.
